nameChecks.en: 'Son, don't forget to go for the heart.'

nameChecks.ja: 死んだ血鬼たちが為の葬儀

gameLocalization.note: Names follow paired Canto IX part 3 enemy, status, and assist records. Guide spacing aliases use Hurting Pest [Roaches] and Protecting Pest [Roaches]. Funeral for a Dead Bloodfiend follows assist skill 40001209. Excision Coins, Unbreakable-based enemy buffs, fixed Heads probability, pest management, NPC targeting, and the 30 HP ending are retained.

lead.text: Have Heathcliff and Rodion handle Gluttony skills and pests while Vergilius supplies major damage and dangerous clashes. Using Unbreakable Coins against Gluttony skills strengthens the enemy, so check the NPC's clash targets before starting.

listLead.text: Heathcliff and Rodion handle Gluttony skills and pests, while the allied NPC handles dangerous clashes and supplies major damage. Using Unbreakable Coins against Gluttony skills strengthens the enemy; check the NPC's clash targets first.

statNote.text: Heathcliff and Rodion are the two required Sinners, fighting alongside Vergilius. Sinners start at 30 SP, or −30 for Identities whose basic attacks all use negative Coins, and share three Ampule uses. Tables show base values without Low Morale, Panic, or HP-loss debuffs. The ending event triggers at 30 HP.

skillNote.text: Excision Coins are special Coins that can destroy Unbreakable Coins. They are distinguished from ordinary Unbreakable Coins in skill labels and effects. The enemy's Heads chance is fixed at 50% regardless of SP, so do not choose clashers from favorable predictions alone.

priorities.0.text: Assign Sinner skills without Unbreakable Coins to Gluttony attacks.

priorities.1.text: Halve Hurting Pest through Devouring; reduce Protecting Pest by inflicting statuses.

priorities.2.text: Leave the final heart-targeting skill to the NPC; have Sinners handle Excision and Feast.

troubleshooting.0.symptom.text: A Gluttony skill suddenly gains Power when the NPC clashes with it

troubleshooting.0.advice.text: Devouring gains +10 Base Power per opposing Unbreakable Coin; Excision and Feast gain +20. After Vergilius manifests E.G.O, redirect these clashes to Sinner skills with ordinary Coins. Check for skills that become Unbreakable conditionally too.

troubleshooting.1.symptom.text: Sinners die despite having a Shield

troubleshooting.1.advice.text: Hurting Pest reduces max HP and deals fixed damage equal to stacks × 12 at Combat Start. At 50, that is 600 damage, consuming the support Shield. Let Devouring hit to halve stacks before they build up, and avoid concentrating several strong attacks on one Sinner.

troubleshooting.2.symptom.text: The later major attack wipes the party

troubleshooting.2.advice.text: Check whether Vergilius is clashing with The Emperor's Excision. Redirect that Gluttony skill to a Sinner, but preserve the NPC's Funeral clash against 'Son, don't forget to go for the heart.'. Do not swap these assignments.

phases.0.title.text: Bring two Sinners who can take Blunt hits and use ordinary Coins

phases.0.steps.0.text: Recommended Lv. 60. Only Heathcliff and Rodion are controllable. Prioritize Blunt resistance and HP/SP recovery.

phases.0.steps.1.text: Inflicting Burn, Bleed, Tremor, Rupture, or Sinking reduces Protecting Pest. Your role is to supply status amounts rather than defeat the enemy through status damage alone.

phases.0.steps.2.text: Save ordinary-Coin attacks for Gluttony skills. Even a strong skill is unsuitable if its Coins become Unbreakable when conditions are met.

phases.1.title.text: Sinners handle weaker skills and Gluttony; the NPC handles dangerous skills

phases.1.steps.0.text: Through The Guide, assigning a Sinner attack to the skill Vergilius is handling moves him to another unassigned skill. Removing the attack moves him back, so check the final clash lines before starting.

phases.1.steps.1.text: Assign relatively manageable skills such as the Lust Fist and Gluttony attacks to Sinners; leave Flogging and Quaking to the NPC. Do not pile several strong attacks onto one Sinner.

phases.1.steps.2.text: When a Sinner loses a clash, the Emperor loses 5 SP and deals less damage to Sinners. Even an unwinnable clash can help, but only if HP, pests, and Shields allow survival.

phases.1.steps.3.text: Low Morale applies 8 Clash Power Down and 3 Power Down; Panic applies 10 and 5, greatly weakening the enemy. Heads chance stays at 50%, so use strong regular skills or E.G.O even at low enemy SP.

phases.2.title.text: Choose who takes Devouring to halve their pests

phases.2.steps.0.text: Assign The Emperor's Devouring to a Sinner with high Hurting Pest. On hit, it halves pests and grants resources according to the reduction. Around 35 is a warning sign; do not leave stacks to reach the cap of 50.

phases.2.steps.1.text: Devouring also absorbs the target's negative effects. Absorbed Burn and similar statuses reduce Protecting Pest, combining pest management with preparation to break the enemy Shield.

phases.2.steps.2.text: A hit without Coin destruction also absorbs positive effects. Do not automatically offer a heavily buffed Sinner; check incoming damage and what the enemy will gain.

phases.3.title.text: Create an opening and have a Sinner handle the Shield

phases.3.steps.0.text: Inflict Potency and Count of the five statuses to reduce Protecting Pest. At 0, the enemy gains 10 Defense Level Down instead of Protecting Pest next turn, creating an opening.

phases.3.steps.1.text: If The Emperor's Shield designates the NPC, it reduces damage from his attacks by 50%. Have a Sinner take over to preserve NPC damage.

phases.3.steps.2.text: This opening is temporary. At Turn End, negative effects are removed and Protecting Pest returns; inflict statuses again to reduce it.

phases.4.title.text: Sinners handle Excision and Feast; the NPC handles the heart-targeting skill

phases.4.steps.0.text: At 50% HP or when Staggered, the pattern changes and Hurting Pest application increases. SP resets to 0 and Protecting Pest to 50, so the first half's debuffs do not simply carry on.

phases.4.steps.1.text: Always assign the Gluttony skills The Emperor's Excision and The Emperor's Feast to Sinner skills without Unbreakable Coins. In particular, letting the NPC clash with the area Excision greatly increases its Power.

phases.4.steps.2.text: An undestroyed second Coin from Feast restores 25% of enemy HP on hit. During Low Morale or Panic, use a high-Power E.G.O if needed to win and prevent that healing.

phases.4.steps.3.text: Leave 'Son, don't forget to go for the heart.' to the NPC's Funeral for a Dead Bloodfiend. Adding a Sinner attack to that target moves the NPC to another skill, so preserve the clash line.

phases.4.steps.4.text: NPC debuffs and other effects can still cause his major skill to fail. Check predictions and applied effects rather than assuming victory, and progress to the event at 30 HP.

mechanics.0.effect.text: The assistant in 9-45. Supplies most damage and strong clashes; The Guide changes his attack targets. You lose if he dies.

mechanics.0.response.text: Redirect Gluttony skills to Sinners and leave the later heart-targeting clash to him.

mechanics.1.effect.text: Maximum 50. Max HP −1% per stack; at Combat Start, take fixed damage equal to stacks × 12. When reduced, gain random resources equal to the stacks removed (max 15).

mechanics.1.response.text: Halved on a hit from Devouring. Choose the Sinner who takes it before stacks reach the cap.

mechanics.2.effect.text: Maximum 50. Prevents application of Burn, Bleed, Tremor, Rupture, and Sinking Potency or Count, losing an equal number of stacks instead. At Turn Start, gain a Shield equal to stacks × 40.

mechanics.2.response.text: Reduce it by inflicting statuses, creating an opening on the turn after it reaches 0.

mechanics.3.effect.text: Can destroy Unbreakable Coins in clashes and still attacks intact after a clash loss. Coin Power becomes 1 after losing.

mechanics.3.response.text: Distinguish Excision Coin's own effect from Gluttony skills gaining Power against opposing Unbreakable Coins.

mechanics.4.effect.text: On lethal damage while another ally lives, clear Stagger and fully restore HP. All allies' remaining counts decrease by 1 simultaneously. The two Sinners share three uses.

mechanics.4.response.text: This is not three revivals each. Do not spend them all on pests and concentrated hits.

mechanics.5.effect.text: Assigning a Sinner attack to the NPC's clash target moves him to another unassigned skill.

mechanics.5.response.text: Leave Gluttony and Shield to Sinners, and the later heart-targeting skill to the NPC.

mechanics.6.effect.text: Each turn, Vergilius replenishes Shields on all allies up to 600.

mechanics.6.response.text: At 50 Hurting Pest, start-of-combat damage is 600. Do not neglect pests even with support available.

mechanics.7.effect.text: The state in which the NPC uses his manifested E.G.O skills. All his skills become Unbreakable from Turn 4.

mechanics.7.response.text: After manifestation, always reassign Gluttony skills to Sinners.

mechanics.8.effect.text: Vergilius's major skill against the late heart-targeting attack.

mechanics.8.response.text: Do not add a Sinner clash against the same target and accidentally change the NPC's assignment.

warnings.0.text: Even a strong E.G.O strengthens Gluttony skills if it has Unbreakable Coins. Check for ordinary Coins.

warnings.1.text: Devouring halves pests on hit. Winning the clash and preventing every hit does not provide the same pest removal.

warnings.2.text: The Emperor's Heads chance remains 50% during Low Morale or Panic. Clash-win probability alone does not guarantee safety.

warnings.3.text: NPC death also causes defeat. Do not leave dangerous Gluttony skills to him, and preserve his heart-targeting clash.

preparation.0.text: Recommended Lv. 60. Prioritize Blunt resistance, healing, and SP management for the two required Sinners.

preparation.1.text: Bring skills that inflict the five statuses and high-Power attacks without Unbreakable Coins.

roles.0.reason.text: Avoid strengthening Gluttony skills and direct the NPC toward dangerous attacks.

roles.1.reason.text: Reduce Protecting Pest to let NPC damage through.

roles.2.reason.text: Preserve shared Ampules and limit start-of-combat damage.

units.0.stagger.text: 50% (1,520) / Pattern changes on reaching this threshold or being Staggered

units.0.notes.0.text: Heads chance is 50% regardless of SP. Plan for Heads even at low SP.

units.0.notes.1.text: At Turn Start, gain a Shield equal to Protecting Pest × 40. At 50 stacks, this is 2,000.

units.0.notes.2.text: At 50% HP or when Staggered, The Emperor's Wrath activates, resetting SP to 0 and Protecting Pest to 50.

units.0.notes.3.text: Cannot fall below 30 HP; the event triggers at 30.

passives.0.effect.text:
Heads chance is fixed at 50% regardless of SP.

On winning a clash against a Sinner, lose 5 SP and deal 40% less damage to Sinners.

In Low Morale or Panic, gain Clash Power Down and Power Down.
On recovering from Panic, gain 2 Power Down.
“But has it really all been unwrapped?”

passives.0.condition.text: Fixed 50% Heads chance; clash wins against Sinners

passives.0.response.text: Assigning Sinners also helps lower SP and reduce damage. Still avoid concentrated hits.

passives.1.effect.text:
At Turn Start, gain 50 Protecting Pest [Roaches] (the amount gained decreases by 3 each turn, up to a reduction of 20).
- If the user has Burn, Bleed, Tremor, Rupture, or Sinking, randomly reduce their Potency and lose Protecting Pest equal to the amount reduced.
- If the effect has 1 Potency and at least 2 Count, reduce Count instead.

If all Protecting Pest is depleted during combat, apply the following next turn:
- Gain 10 Defense Level Down instead of Protecting Pest.
- Generate 2 resources of each of the enemy's three least-abundant E.G.O affinities.
- At Turn End, remove all negative effects and gain Protecting Pest.
Wherever and whenever it may be, they crawl out from the lines where surfaces meet.

passives.1.response.text: Use the five statuses to reduce Protecting Pest and create an opening next turn.

passives.2.effect.text:
At Turn Start, gain a Shield equal to (Protecting Pest [Roaches] × 40).
The swarm moves for one emperor alone.

passives.2.response.text: At 50 Protecting Pest, the Shield is 2,000. Reduce pests before focusing on HP damage.

passives.3.effect.text:
- On Clash Win, inflict 3 Hurting Pest [Roaches] on the target.
- On skill hit, inflict 1 Hurting Pest [Roaches] on the target.
Burrow, seep, permeate, gnaw, tear, and devour.

passives.3.response.text: Avoid building up pests; rotate who takes Devouring to halve them.

passives.4.effect.text:
HP damage, SP damage, and Stagger Threshold advancement from Burn, Bleed, Tremor, Rupture, and Sinking are reduced by 50%.
This damage cannot cause Stagger.
At Turn Start, gain 2 Power Down per 25% HP the main body has lost.
Adapt to everything, and grow dull.

passives.4.response.text: Use status application amounts, as well as direct damage, to strip pests.

passives.5.effect.text:
At 50% HP or when Staggered, clear Stagger among the user's negative effects and change the pattern.
Then apply the following:
- Set SP to 0.
- Gain 50 Protecting Pest [Roaches].
- Double the Hurting Pest [Roaches] inflicted by The Emperor's Legion.

passives.5.response.text: Returns to 0 SP and 50 Protecting Pest, with increased pest application. Reassign clashes for the second-half skills.

passives.6.effect.text: When gaining a buff that changes Panic Type, Panic Type stays unchanged. Apply the effects intended for targets without SP instead.

passives.6.response.text: Use skill assignments and debuffs rather than relying on a different Panic Type.

passives.7.effect.text: If Panicked at Turn End, reset SP to 0.

passives.7.response.text: SP recovers. Do not treat Panic-based weakening as permanent.
